paragraphs.title: God’s Kingship and the Stability of the World

easy.q: What is the LORD clothed with?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved.”
easy.q: What is established so that it cannot be moved?

medium.q: How long has the LORD’s throne been established?

medium.explanation: The LORD is clothed with strength and has girded Himself with it.
medium.q: What has the LORD girded Himself with?

medium.explanation: The LORD’s rule is presented alongside the world being firmly established.
medium.q: What connection is shown between God’s reign and the world?

challenge.explanation: Both phrases point to God’s eternal existence and ancient throne.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by “of old” and “from everlasting”?

challenge.explanation: The LORD is clothed with majesty and strength.
challenge.q: Which pair best describes the LORD’s royal appearance?

challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the world is firmly established.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the statement that the world cannot be moved?

paragraphs.title: The Song of the Rivers and the Sea

easy.explanation: The verse repeats that the floods have lifted up their voice.
easy.q: What has lifted up its voice?

easy.explanation: The floods have lifted up their waves.
easy.q: What have the floods lifted up?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD on high is mightier.”
easy.q: Who is mightier than the noise of many waters?

medium.explanation: The passage speaks of “the mighty waves of the sea.”
medium.q: What is described as mighty in the passage?

medium.explanation: The LORD on high is mightier than the waters’ noise.
medium.q: What is greater than the noise of many waters?

medium.explanation: The floods repeatedly lift up their voice and waves.
medium.q: How does the passage portray the floods?

answers: It emphasizes their power and movement
challenge.explanation: The repetition draws attention to the floods’ forceful motion and sound.
challenge.q: What effect does the repetition about the floods create?

answers: The mighty waters versus the mightier LORD
challenge.explanation: Even the mighty waters are surpassed by the LORD’s power.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The word means greater in strength or power.

paragraphs.title: The Faithfulness of God’s Testimonies and the Holiness of His House

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thy testimonies are very sure.”
easy.q: How are the LORD’s testimonies described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “holiness becometh thine house.”

easy.q: How long is holiness said to belong to God’s house?

medium.q: What does “very sure” communicate about God’s testimonies?

answers: Holiness is fitting for God’s house
The house belongs to the sea
medium.explanation: The wording says that holiness is appropriate for God’s house.
medium.q: What does “becometh thine house” mean in context?

medium.explanation: The verse moves from God’s sure testimonies to His holy house and its enduring character.
medium.q: What is the order of ideas in the verse?

challenge.explanation: In context, testimonies refer to God’s revealed declarations and instruction.
challenge.q: Which meaning best fits “testimonies” in this verse?

answers: God’s truth is reliable and enduring
God’s truth depends on the floods
challenge.explanation: The verse joins certainty with lasting permanence.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between “very sure” and “for ever”?

challenge.explanation: “Becometh” means that holiness is fitting or appropriate for God’s house.
challenge.q: Which KJV word means “suitable” or “fitting” in this verse?
